message.content:
**Order filled:** 25 shares of AMZN at $195.30 = $4,882.50.

**Summary:** I read Amazon.com's fiscal 2023 Form 10-K (year ended 2023-12-31) and found a clear, broad-based improvement in the business: total net sales of $574,785M (up ~11.8% from $513,983M in 2022), operating income of $36,852M (roughly tripled from $12,248M), net income of $30,425M versus a $2,722M loss the prior year, diluted EPS of $2.90 versus -$0.27, and operating cash flow of $84,946M — a strong cash-generating franchise with a healthy balance-sheet liquidity statement. The filing's risk factors (global economic conditions, supply chains, customer demand) and routine litigation are generic and did not change the thesis. With the quote at $195.25 (bid $195.23 / ask $195.27), I sized the position at 25 shares (~$4,882) to stay under the $5,000 per-order cap — 26 shares would have breached it at ~$5,076 — and placed a single buy limit at $195.30, essentially at market, which filled at $195.30. This is well within the $10,000 daily limit (total traded today: $4,882.50), uses only existing cash (no money moved out of the account), and stays inside the AMZN/HD, buy-only mandate. I did not touch the existing 50-share HD position.
